Quellen: <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=11">AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface §1.1 „AUTOSAR CAN Layer Model“</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00023" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00023">[SWS_CANIF_00023]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00033" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00033">[SWS_CanTp_00033]</a></p> <h4>Zusammenspiel &amp; Interaktionspfade zwischen den Modulen</h4> <p>Der Sendevorgang für unsegmentierte Frames beginnt bei oberen Modulen oder für segmentierte Diagnosedaten bei <code>cantp</code> über den Aufruf von <code>CanIf_Transmit()</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00005" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00005">[SWS_CANIF_00005]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00216" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00216">[SWS_CanTp_00216]</a>. <code>canif</code> überprüft zunächst, ob sich der referenzierte Controller im Modus <code>CAN_CS_STARTED</code> befindet und der PDU-Kanal aktiv geschaltet ist <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00317" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00317">[SWS_CANIF_00317]</a>. Anhand der statisch konfigurierten PDU-Zuordnung ermittelt <code>canif</code> das zuständige Hardware Transmit Handle (HTH) <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=31">AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface §7.2 „Hardware object handles“</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00292" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00292">[SWS_CANIF_00292]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00318" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00318">[SWS_CANIF_00318]</a> und leitet das Paket an <code>Can_Write()</code> im Modul <code>can</code> weiter <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00233" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00233">[SWS_Can_00233]</a>. Falls alle Hardware-Objekte belegt sind und <code>Can_Write()</code> den Status <code>CAN_BUSY</code> meldet, puffert <code>canif</code> die Sendeanforderung bei aktiver Pufferung im <code>CanIfTxBuffer</code> prioritätsbasiert nach CAN-Identifier <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00039" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00039">[SWS_Can_00039]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00063" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00063">[SWS_CANIF_00063]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00070" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00070">[SWS_CANIF_00070]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00381" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00381">[SWS_CANIF_00381]</a>.</p> <p>Sobald der Controller das Frame erfolgreich auf dem Bus abgesetzt hat, meldet <code>can</code> den Abschluss via <code>CanIf_TxConfirmation()</code> an <code>canif</code> zurück <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00007" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00007">[SWS_CANIF_00007]</a>. <code>canif</code> identifiziert das zugehörige Zielmodul und ruft die konfigurierte Bestätigungs-Callback-Funktion auf, beispielsweise <code>CanTp_TxConfirmation()</code> für Transportprotokolle oder <code>PduR_CanIfTxConfirmation()</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00383" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00383">[SWS_CANIF_00383]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00438" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00438">[SWS_CANIF_00438]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00439" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00439">[SWS_CANIF_00439]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00550" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00550">[SWS_CANIF_00550]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00076" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00076">[SWS_CanTp_00076]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00215" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00215">[SWS_CanTp_00215]</a>. Direkt im Anschluss prüft <code>canif</code>, ob weitere L-PDUs im Sendepuffer anstehen, und übergibt das nächste priorisierte Frame unmittelbar an <code>Can_Write()</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00183" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00183">[SWS_CANIF_00183]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00386" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00386">[SWS_CANIF_00386]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00668" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00668">[SWS_CANIF_00668]</a>.</p> <p>Auf dem Empfangspfad signalisiert <code>can</code> eingehende Botschaften unter Angabe des Hardware Receive Handle (HRH) über <code>CanIf_RxIndication()</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00006" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00006">[SWS_CANIF_00006]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00291" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00291">[SWS_CANIF_00291]</a>. In <code>canif</code> durchläuft das Frame bei BasicCAN-Mailboxen eine konfigurierte Software-Filterung gegen Masken oder ID-Bereiche <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00030" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00030">[SWS_CANIF_00030]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00211" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00211">[SWS_CANIF_00211]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00389" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00389">[SWS_CANIF_00389]</a>. Besteht das Paket die Filterung, prüft <code>canif</code> die Datenlänge (Data Length Check) <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00026" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00026">[SWS_CANIF_00026]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00390" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00390">[SWS_CANIF_00390]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00902" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00902">[SWS_CANIF_00902]</a> und routet die Nutzdaten an das vorgesehene Zielmodul weiter, wie <code>CanTp_RxIndication()</code> oder <code>PduR_CanIfRxIndication()</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00442" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00442">[SWS_CANIF_00442]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00448" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00448">[SWS_CANIF_00448]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00078" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00078">[SWS_CanTp_00078]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00214" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00214">[SWS_CanTp_00214]</a>.</p> <p>Im Modul <code>cantp</code> erfolgt die Abwicklung segmentierter Transporte nach ISO 15765-2 mittels Single Frame (SF), First Frame (FF), Consecutive Frame (CF) und Flow Control (FC) <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00035" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00035">[SWS_CanTp_00035]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00282" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00282">[SWS_CanTp_00282]</a>. Beim Empfang eines FF fragt <code>cantp</code> über <code>PduR_CanTpStartOfReception()</code> Puffer beim PduR an <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00064" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00064">[SWS_CanTp_00064]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00079" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00079">[SWS_CanTp_00079]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00080" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00080">[SWS_CanTp_00080]</a>, übermittelt ein FC-Frame via <code>CanIf_Transmit()</code> und kopiert sukzessive CF-Nutzdaten mit <code>PduR_CanTpCopyRxData()</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00269" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00269">[SWS_CanTp_00269]</a>, bevor die Session mit <code>PduR_CanTpRxIndication()</code> abgeschlossen wird <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00084" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00084">[SWS_CanTp_00084]</a>. Beim Senden holt <code>cantp</code> segmentweise Daten via <code>PduR_CanTpCopyTxData()</code> ab <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00086" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00086">[SWS_CanTp_00086]</a>, da <code>cantp</code> keine statischen Nutzdatenpuffer vorhält <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00298" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00298">[SWS_CanTp_00298]</a>, und schließt den Transfer über <code>PduR_CanTpTxConfirmation()</code> ab <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00090" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00090">[SWS_CanTp_00090]</a>.</p> <div class="diagram" id="diag-can-interaction"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewbox="0 0 900 760" Empfangsabläufen. Quellen: <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00212" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00212">[SWS_CanTp_00212]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00005" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00005">[SWS_CANIF_00005]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00233" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00233">[SWS_Can_00233]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00006" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00006">[SWS_CANIF_00006]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00214" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00214">[SWS_CanTp_00214]</a></p> <h4>Synchronisation, Reentranz und Task-Kontexte</h4> <p>Das Modulcluster unterstützt sowohl interruptgesteuerte als auch pollingbasierte Betriebsmodi. Im Polling-Betrieb stellt das Modul <code>can</code> periodische Hauptfunktionen bereit: <code>Can_MainFunction_Write()</code> zur Überprüfung vollendeter Sendeaufträge <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00225" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00225">[SWS_Can_00225]</a>, <code>Can_MainFunction_Read()</code> zum Abholen empfangener Frames <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00226" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00226">[SWS_Can_00226]</a>, <code>Can_MainFunction_BusOff()</code> zur Erkennung von Bus-Off-Zuständen <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00227" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00227">[SWS_Can_00227]</a>, <code>Can_MainFunction_Wakeup()</code> für Wakeup-Ereignisse <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00228" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00228">[SWS_Can_00228]</a> sowie <code>Can_MainFunction_Mode()</code> für Controller-Moduswechsel <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00368" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00368">[SWS_Can_00368]</a>. Das Modul <code>cantp</code> verfügt über <code>CanTp_MainFunction()</code>, welche im Zyklus von <code>CanTpMainFunctionPeriod</code> aufgerufen wird und Protokoll-Timer wie N_As, N_Bs, N_Cs, N_Ar, N_Br und N_Cr überwacht <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00075" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00075">[SWS_CanTp_00075]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00164" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00164">[SWS_CanTp_00164]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00166" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00166">[SWS_CanTp_00166]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00167" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00167">[SWS_CanTp_00167]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00213" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00213">[SWS_CanTp_00213]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00300" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00300">[SWS_CanTp_00300]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00312" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00312">[SWS_CanTp_00312]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00315" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00315">[SWS_CanTp_00315]</a>. In <code>cantrcv</code> scannt <code>CanTrcv_MainFunction()</code> die Transceiverkanäle in Standby und Sleep zyklisch auf Wakeup-Ereignisse <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTrcv_00013" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTrcv_00013">[SWS_CanTrcv_00013]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTrcv_00112" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTrcv_00112">[SWS_CanTrcv_00112]</a>, während <code>CanTrcv_MainFunctionDiagnostics()</code> Busfehlerflags ausliest <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTrcv_00205" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTrcv_00205">[SWS_CanTrcv_00205]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTrcv_00218" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTrcv_00218">[SWS_CanTrcv_00218]</a>.</p> <p>Im Interrupt-Betrieb dürfen Callbacks wie <code>CanIf_RxIndication()</code>, <code>CanIf_TxConfirmation()</code> sowie die korrespondierenden <code>CanTp_RxIndication()</code> und <code>CanTp_TxConfirmation()</code> direkt aus dem Interrupt-Kontext des Treibers aufgerufen werden <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00235" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00235">[SWS_CanTp_00235]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00236" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00236">[SWS_CanTp_00236]</a>. Bedienen mehrere Instanzen von <code>can</code> unterschiedliche Interruptvektoren, müssen alle Callback-Routinen in <code>canif</code> reentrant ausgelegt sein <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../spec/record.html?doc=AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface&amp;page=20">AUTOSAR_SWS_CANInterface §5 „Overview“</a>. Zur Vermeidung von Dateninkonsistenzen schützt <code>canif</code> kritische Abschnitte, insbesondere den nebenläufigen Zugriff auf <code>CanIfTxBuffer</code> und die Rekonfiguration dynamischer CAN-IDs in <code>CanIf_SetDynamicTxId()</code>, gegen präemptive Unterbrechungen <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00033" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00033">[SWS_CANIF_00033]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00064" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00064">[SWS_CANIF_00064]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00673" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00673">[SWS_CANIF_00673]</a>. Controller-Interrupts können im Bedarfsfall über <code>Can_DisableControllerInterrupts()</code> gesperrt und mit <code>Can_EnableControllerInterrupts()</code> wieder freigegeben werden <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00231" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00231">[SWS_Can_00231]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00232" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00232">[SWS_Can_00232]</a>.</p> <p>Hinsichtlich Multicore- und Partitionierungsarchitekturen gilt für <code>can</code> und <code>cantrcv</code> eine strikte Zuordnung: Instanzen arbeiten partitionsspezifisch unabhängig voneinander, wobei API-Aufrufe stets an die aufrufende Partition gebunden bleiben <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_CONSTR_00508" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_CONSTR_00508">[SWS_Can_CONSTR_00508]</a>. Controller und Transceiver desselben physikalischen Kanals müssen zwingend derselben ECUC-Partition zugeordnet sein, andernfalls wird die Konfiguration zurückgewiesen <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_CONSTR_00510" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_CONSTR_00510">[SWS_Can_CONSTR_00510]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTrcv_00231" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTrcv_00231">[SWS_CanTrcv_00231]</a>.</p> <h4>Typische Lebenszyklen und Betriebsmodi</h4> <p>Beim Systemhochlauf befinden sich die Module zunächst im Zustand <code>CAN_CS_UNINIT</code> bzw. <code>CANTP_OFF</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91013" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91013">[SWS_Can_91013]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00168" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00168">[SWS_CanTp_00168]</a>. Der ECU State Manager (EcuM) initialisiert die Treiber in definierter Reihenfolge: <code>Can_Init()</code> konfiguriert die Hardware-Register und überführt alle Controller in <code>CAN_CS_STOPPED</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00223" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00223">[SWS_Can_00223]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91012" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91012">[SWS_Can_91012]</a>; <code>CanTrcv_Init()</code> initialisiert die Bustransceiver und versetzt sie je nach Konfiguration in Standby oder Sleep <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTrcv_00001" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTrcv_00001">[SWS_CanTrcv_00001]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTrcv_00148" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTrcv_00148">[SWS_CanTrcv_00148]</a>. Danach initialisiert <code>CanIf_Init()</code> globale Tabellen und Puffer, schaltet alle Kanäle auf <code>CANIF_OFFLINE</code> und aktiviert etwaige Partial-Networking-Filter <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00085" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00085">[SWS_CANIF_00085]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00387" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00387">[SWS_CANIF_00387]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00863" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00863">[SWS_CANIF_00863]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00864" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00864">[SWS_CANIF_00864]</a>. Zuletzt schaltet <code>CanTp_Init()</code> das Transportprotokoll in den betriebsbereiten Zustand <code>CANTP_ON</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00030" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00030">[SWS_CanTp_00030]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00170" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00170">[SWS_CanTp_00170]</a>.</p> <p>Im laufenden Betrieb koordiniert der CAN State Manager (CanSM) die Betriebsmodi der Controller und PDU-Kanäle. Modusanforderungen werden über <code>CanIf_SetControllerMode()</code> eingesteuert und mittels <code>Can_SetControllerMode()</code> an die Hardware übergeben <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00003" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00003">[SWS_CANIF_00003]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00230" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00230">[SWS_Can_00230]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00308" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00308">[SWS_CANIF_00308]</a>. Gültige Zustände sind <code>CAN_CS_STOPPED</code>, <code>CAN_CS_STARTED</code> und <code>CAN_CS_SLEEP</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91013" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91013">[SWS_Can_91013]</a>. Bestätigungen leitet <code>canif</code> via <code>CanIf_ControllerModeIndication()</code> an CanSM weiter <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00699" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00699">[SWS_CANIF_00699]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00711" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00711">[SWS_CANIF_00711]</a>. Unabhängig vom Controller-Zustand steuert <code>CanIf_SetPduMode()</code> den PDU-Kanal-Modus: <code>CANIF_OFFLINE</code> unterbindet Senden und Empfangen, <code>CANIF_TX_OFFLINE</code> sperrt nur den Sendepfad, <code>CANIF_ONLINE</code> gibt die Kommunikation vollständig frei, und <code>CANIF_TX_OFFLINE_ACTIVE</code> simuliert Sendeübertragungen durch rein internes Auslösen der Tx-Confirmations ohne Busaktivität <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00008" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00008">[SWS_CANIF_00008]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00072" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00072">[SWS_CANIF_00072]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00073" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00073">[SWS_CANIF_00073]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00075" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00075">[SWS_CANIF_00075]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00137" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00137">[SWS_CANIF_00137]</a>. Ein Wechsel in <code>CAN_CS_STOPPED</code> leert automatisch alle anstehenden Sendepuffer <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00485" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00485">[SWS_CANIF_00485]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00866" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00866">[SWS_CANIF_00866]</a>.</p> <p>Transceiver werden über <code>CanIf_SetTrcvMode()</code> und <code>CanTrcv_SetOpMode()</code> zwischen <code>CANTRCV_TRCVMODE_NORMAL</code>, <code>CANTRCV_TRCVMODE_STANDBY</code> und <code>CANTRCV_TRCVMODE_SLEEP</code> geschaltet <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00287" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00287">[SWS_CANIF_00287]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTrcv_00002" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTrcv_00002">[SWS_CanTrcv_00002]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTrcv_00102" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTrcv_00102">[SWS_CanTrcv_00102]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTrcv_00163" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTrcv_00163">[SWS_CanTrcv_00163]</a>, woraufhin <code>cantrcv</code> die Umschaltung mit <code>CanIf_TrcvModeIndication()</code> bestätigt <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTrcv_00158" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTrcv_00158">[SWS_CanTrcv_00158]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00712" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00712">[SWS_CANIF_00712]</a>. Im Sleep-Modus werden Wakeup-Ereignisse über <code>CanIf_CheckWakeup()</code> an <code>Can_CheckWakeup()</code> bzw. <code>CanTrcv_CheckWakeup()</code> delegiert <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00219" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00219">[SWS_CANIF_00219]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00395" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00395">[SWS_CANIF_00395]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00360" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00360">[SWS_Can_00360]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTrcv_00143" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTrcv_00143">[SWS_CanTrcv_00143]</a> und optional mit <code>CanIf_CheckValidation()</code> validiert <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00178" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00178">[SWS_CANIF_00178]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00286" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00286">[SWS_CANIF_00286]</a>. Bei Partial Networking (PN) blockiert ein aktivierter <code>PnTxFilter</code> in <code>canif</code> alle Sendeanforderungen, bis ein gültiges Rx-Frame oder eine erfolgreiche Tx-Confirmation den Filter aufhebt <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00747" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00747">[SWS_CANIF_00747]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00749" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00749">[SWS_CANIF_00749]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00750" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00750">[SWS_CANIF_00750]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00751" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00751">[SWS_CANIF_00751]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00896" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00896">[SWS_CANIF_00896]</a>, während <code>cantrcv</code> selektive Wakeup-Muster auswertet und Flags über <code>CanIf_ClearTrcvWufFlag()</code> bereinigt <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00760" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00760">[SWS_CANIF_00760]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTrcv_00174" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTrcv_00174">[SWS_CanTrcv_00174]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTrcv_00194" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTrcv_00194">[SWS_CanTrcv_00194]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTrcv_00219" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTrcv_00219">[SWS_CanTrcv_00219]</a>.</p> <p>Beim Herunterfahren des Steuergeräts schließt <code>CanTp_Shutdown()</code> alle laufenden Verbindungen und versetzt <code>cantp</code> zurück in den Zustand <code>CANTP_OFF</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00202" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00202">[SWS_CanTp_00202]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00211" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00211">[SWS_CanTp_00211]</a>. Nachfolgend deinitialisieren <code>CanIf_DeInit()</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_91002" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_91002">[SWS_CANIF_91002]</a>, <code>CanTrcv_DeInit()</code> (Wechsel nach <code>NOT_ACTIVE</code>) <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTrcv_91001" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTrcv_91001">[SWS_CanTrcv_91001]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTrcv_91003" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTrcv_91003">[SWS_CanTrcv_91003]</a> und <code>Can_DeInit()</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91002" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91002">[SWS_Can_91002]</a> die jeweiligen Hardwareeinheiten und Datenstrukturen.</p> <h4>Fehlerbehandlung, Det-Tracing und Degradation</h4> <p>Ein zentraler Fehlermechanismus auf dem CAN-Bus ist der Bus-Off-Zustand, der eintritt, wenn der controllerinterne Sendezähler den Schwellenwert von 255 überschreitet. Das Modul <code>can</code> erkennt dies und ruft <code>CanIf_ControllerBusOff()</code> auf <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00234" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00234">[SWS_Can_00234]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00218" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00218">[SWS_CANIF_00218]</a>. <code>canif</code> schaltet den betroffenen Kanal sofort in den Modus <code>CANIF_TX_OFFLINE</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00866" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00866">[SWS_CANIF_00866]</a>, verwirft alle gepufferten Tx-PDUs <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00485" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00485">[SWS_CANIF_00485]</a> und benachrichtigt CanSM via <code>CanSM_ControllerBusOff()</code> zur Einleitung der Bus-Off-Recovery <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00559" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00559">[SWS_CANIF_00559]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00724" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00724">[SWS_CANIF_00724]</a>. Ist Security-Event-Reporting konfiguriert, wird zusätzlich das Sicherheitsereignis <code>CANIF_SEV_ERRORSTATE_BUSOFF</code> erfasst <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00918" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00918">[SWS_CANIF_00918]</a>. Der aktuelle Controller-Fehlerzustand (Active, Passive, Bus-Off) sowie Fehlerzählerstände lassen sich über <code>CanIf_GetControllerErrorState()</code>, <code>CanIf_GetControllerRxErrorCounter()</code> und <code>CanIf_GetControllerTxErrorCounter()</code> diagnostizieren <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91003" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91003">[SWS_Can_91003]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91004" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91004">[SWS_Can_91004]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00511" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00511">[SWS_Can_00511]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_00516" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_00516">[SWS_Can_00516]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_91001" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_91001">[SWS_CANIF_91001]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_91003" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_91003">[SWS_CANIF_91003]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_91004" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_91004">[SWS_CANIF_91004]</a>.</p> <p>Entwicklungsfehler werden bei aktiviertem Default Error Tracer (DET) an den Schnittstellen abgefangen. Hierzu zählen Aufrufe vor erfolgter Modulinitialisierung (<code>CANTP_E_UNINIT</code> in <code>cantp</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00031" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00031">[SWS_CanTp_00031]</a>, Ablehnung mit <code>E_NOT_OK</code> in <code>canif</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00661" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00661">[SWS_CANIF_00661]</a> sowie Fehlerprüfung in <code>cantrcv</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTrcv_00122" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTrcv_00122">[SWS_CanTrcv_00122]</a>) sowie ungültige Parameterwerte. Beispiele sind unzulässige Controller-IDs (<code>CANIF_E_PARAM_CONTROLLERID</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00311" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00311">[SWS_CANIF_00311]</a>), Nullzeiger (<code>CANIF_E_PARAM_POINTER</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00320" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00320">[SWS_CANIF_00320]</a>), fehlerhafte Hardware-Handles (<code>CANIF_E_PARAM_HOH</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00416" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00416">[SWS_CANIF_00416]</a>) und ungültige Transceiver-Nummern (<code>CANTRCV_E_INVALID_TRANSCEIVER</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTrcv_00050" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTrcv_00050">[SWS_CanTrcv_00050]</a>). In <code>cantp</code> werden unzulässige PDU-Identifier oder Parameter via <code>Det_ReportError()</code> protokolliert und Anforderungen abgewiesen <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00217" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00217">[SWS_CanTp_00217]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00293" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00293">[SWS_CanTp_00293]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00294" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00294">[SWS_CanTp_00294]</a>.</p> <p>Laufzeitfehler und Degradationsmechanismen gewährleisten die geordnete Fehlerbehandlung im Serienbetrieb: Scheitert in <code>canif</code> der Data Length Check, meldet das Modul den Laufzeitfehler <code>CANIF_E_INVALID_DATA_LENGTH</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00168" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00168">[SWS_CANIF_00168]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_91007" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_91007">[SWS_CANIF_91007]</a>; Sendeversuche auf gestoppten Kanälen quittiert <code>canif</code> mit <code>CANIF_E_STOPPED</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CANIF_00382" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CANIF_00382">[SWS_CANIF_00382]</a>. Hardware-Überläufe im Controller werden mit <code>CAN_E_DATALOST</code> signalisiert <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_Can_91020" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_Can_91020">[SWS_Can_91020]</a>, während Transceiver-Kommunikationsstörungen zu <code>CANTRCV_E_NO_TRCV_CONTROL</code> führen <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTrcv_00113" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTrcv_00113">[SWS_CanTrcv_00113]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTrcv_91006" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTrcv_91006">[SWS_CanTrcv_91006]</a>. Tritt ein anhaltender Busfehler auf, setzt <code>cantrcv</code> über <code>CanTrcv_MainFunctionDiagnostics()</code> den Fehlerspeicher-Eintrag <code>CANTRCV_E_BUS_ERROR</code> im Diagnostic Event Manager (DEM) via <code>Dem_SetEventStatus()</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTrcv_00206" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTrcv_00206">[SWS_CanTrcv_00206]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTrcv_00227" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTrcv_00227">[SWS_CanTrcv_00227]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTrcv_00228" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTrcv_00228">[SWS_CanTrcv_00228]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTrcv_00229" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTrcv_00229">[SWS_CanTrcv_00229]</a>. Im Transportprotokoll <code>cantp</code> führen Timeouts (N_As, N_Bs, N_Cr) oder Pufferengpässe (<code>BUFREQ_E_NOT_OK</code>, <code>BUFREQ_E_OVFL</code>) zum kontrollierten Sitzungsabbruch und zur Benachrichtigung des PduR mit <code>E_NOT_OK</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00087" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00087">[SWS_CanTp_00087]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00205" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00205">[SWS_CanTp_00205]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00309" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00309">[SWS_CanTp_00309]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00310" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00310">[SWS_CanTp_00310]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00313" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00313">[SWS_CanTp_00313]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00316" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00316">[SWS_CanTp_00316]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00318" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00318">[SWS_CanTp_00318]</a>. Zudem gestattet <code>cantp</code> den geordneten Abbruch laufender Übertragungen auf Anforderung der oberen Schichten via <code>CanTp_CancelTransmit()</code> bzw. <code>CanTp_CancelReceive()</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00243" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00243">[SWS_CanTp_00243]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00246" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00246">[SWS_CanTp_00246]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00257" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00257">[SWS_CanTp_00257]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_CanTp_00261" href="../spec/record.html?id=SWS_CanTp_00261">[SWS_CanTp_00261]</a>.</p> <p class="ai-note">Dieser Leitfaden fasst die Kernarchitektur, Interaktionsmuster und Betriebszustände des CAN-Communication-Clusters gemäß den Vorgaben von AUTOSAR Classic Platform Release R20-11 zusammen.</p> </div>

Figure 1.1: AUTOSAR CAN Layer Model (see [7]) The CAN Interface module consists of all CAN hardware independent tasks, which belongs to the CAN communication device drivers of the corresponding ECU. Those functionality is implemented once in the CAN Interface module, so that underlying CAN device drivers only focus on access and control of the corresponding specific CAN hardware device. CanIf fulfils main control flow and data flow requirements of the PDU Router and upper layer communication modules of the AUTOSAR COM stack: transmit request processing , transmit confirmation / receive indication / error notification and start / stop of a CAN Controller and thus waking up / participating on a network . Its data processing and notification API is based on CAN L-SDUs , whereas APIs for control and mode handling provides a CAN Controller related view. In case of Transmit Requests CanIf completes the L-PDU transmission with cor- responding parameters and relays the CAN L-PDU via the appropriate CanDrv to

The CanDrv detects and processes events of the CAN Controllers and notifies those to the CanIf. The CanIf passes operation mode requests of the CanSm to the corresponding under- lying CAN Controllers. CanDrv provides a normalized L-PDU to ensure hardware independence of CanIf . The pointer to this normalized L-PDU points either to a temporary buffer (for e.g. data normalizing) or to the CAN hardware dependent CanDrv . For CanIf the kind of L-PDU buffer is invisible. The CanIf provides notification services used by the CanDrv in all notifications sce- narios, for example: transmit confirmation (subsection 8.4.2 CanIf_TxConfirmation, see [SWS_CANIF_00007]), receive indication (subsection 8.4.3 CanIf_RxIndication, see [SWS_CANIF_00006]) and notification of a controller mode change (subsection 8.4.8, see [SWS_CANIF_00699]). In case of using multiple CanDrv serving different interrupt vectors these callback ser- vices mentioned above must be re-entrant, refer to section 7.24 Multiple CAN Driver support. 7.2 Hardware object handles Hardware Object Handles ( HOH ) for transmission ( HTH ) as well as for reception ( HRH ) represent an abstract reference to a CAN mailbox structure , that contains CAN related parameters such as CanId , DLC and data . Based on the CAN hardware buffer abstraction each Hardware Object is referenced in CanIf independent of the CAN hardware buffer layout. The HOH is used as a parameter in the calls of CanDrv 's interface services and is provided by CanDrv 's configuration and used by CanDrv as identifier for communication buffers of the CAN mailbox. CanIf acts only as user of the Hardware Object Handle , but does not interpret it on the basis of hardware specific information. CanIf therefore remains independent of hardware. [SWS_CANIF_00023] ⌈ CanIf shall avoid direct access to hardware specific commu- nication buffers and shall access it exclusively via CanDrv interface services. ⌋ (SRS_- Can_01001) Rationale for [SWS_CANIF_00023]: CanIf remains independent of hardware, be- cause CanDrv interfaces are called with HOH parameters, which abstract from the concrete CAN hardware buffer properties. CanIf supports activation and deactivation of all L-PDUs belonging to one CAN Con- troller for transmission as well as for reception (see 7.19.2, see CanIf_SetPdu- Mode() , [SWS_CANIF_00008]). For L-PDU mode control refer to section 7.19. Each L-PDU is associated with an upper layer module in order to ensure correct dis- patching during reception, transmission confirmation, and data access. Each upper layer module can use the L-PDUs to serve different CAN Controllers simultane- ously. According to the PDU architecture defined for the entire AUTOSAR communication stack (see [7, Layered Software Architecture]), the usage of L-PDUs is split in two different ways: • For transmission request and transmission/reception polling API the upper layer module uses the L-SDU ID ( CanTxPduId / CanRxPduId ) defined by CanIf as parameter. • For all callback APIs, which are invoked by CanIf at upper layer modules, CanIf passes the target PduId defined by each upper layer module as parameter. The principle is that the caller must use the defined target L-PDU / L-SDU Id of the callee. If power on initialization is not performed and upper layer performs transmit requests to CanIf , no L-SDUs are tran…

Figure 7.3: Physical channel view definition example B 7.6 CAN Hardware Unit The CAN Hardware Unit combines one or multiple CAN Controller modules of the same type, which may be located on-chip or as external standalone devices. Each CAN Hardware Unit is served by the corresponding CanDrv . If different types of CAN Controllers are used, also different types of CanDrvs have to be applied with a unified API to CanIf . CanIf collects information about number and types of CAN Controllers and their Hardware Objects at configuration time. This allows transparent and hardware independent access to the CAN Controllers from upper layer modules using HOHs (refer to section 7.2 Hardware object handles and section 7.24 Multiple CAN Driver support).
